fields.meta_description: What a direct deposit form asks for, where to get one, and an app that checks routing numbers and confirms every bank change.
fields.h1: Build a Direct Deposit Form That Checks Bank Details
fields.hero_description: A direct deposit form tells payroll which bank account receives each paycheck. Describe how your team collects bank details, and Emergent builds the form and the checks behind it.
fields.features_heading: What a Direct Deposit Form Should Catch
fields.features_subheading: A direct deposit form PDF records the numbers. Emergent's version checks them before the first payday.
fields.feature_1:
Routing numbers checked on entry

Runs the check-digit math on each nine-digit routing number the moment it is entered. A transposed digit gets caught on the form, long before it turns into a returned deposit.
fields.feature_2:
Voided checks read into the form

Reads the routing and account numbers off an uploaded voided check or bank letter, then compares them with what the employee typed. Any digit that differs goes back to them.
fields.feature_3:
Pay split across several accounts

Lets employees route part of each paycheck to a second or third account by dollar amount or percentage. The form refuses to submit until one account is set to take the remainder.
fields.feature_4:
Bank changes held until confirmed

Keeps every request to switch a deposit account on hold until the employee approves it from contact details HR already had. Nothing reaches the payroll export while it waits.
fields.feature_5:
Account numbers shown as the last four

Shows only the last four digits of each account number on the dashboard and in alerts. The full number stays in a database you own, open to the payroll admins you name.
fields.feature_6:
A payroll sync whenever you want one

Exports the full code to your GitHub repo. An engineer can add a nightly push to your payroll provider's API, or you can describe the change and let Emergent write it.

fields.usecase_heading: Direct Deposit Forms for Every Payee
fields.tab_content_1:
The wrong digit caught before payday

New hires type the routing and account numbers, then upload a voided check. Emergent reads the check and compares its numbers with the typed ones. If the routing number does not match, the form goes back to the new hire with that field marked. Payroll only receives records that agree.
fields.tab_content_2:
A fixed $150 to savings, the rest to checking

Plenty of employees keep a savings goal that comes out of every paycheck. Each extra account takes a fixed amount or a percentage, and one account is marked for the remainder. On a sample net pay of $2,140, the employee sees $150 land in savings and $1,990 in checking.
fields.tab_content_3:
No new account until the employee confirms

Payroll fraud rarely starts in payroll. A stolen login or a spoofed email asks to switch the deposit account. Emergent holds the change and emails a confirmation link to the address on file. Once the employee confirms, the payroll manager gets a Slack direct message naming the employee.
fields.tab_content_4:
Bank details and a W-9 in one submission

Contractors get paid by ACH too, and accounts payable needs a taxpayer ID first. The form collects bank details and the W-9 together, then compares the account holder's name with the W-9 name. When they differ, the contractor waits for accounts payable review before joining the next payout run.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Direct Deposit Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work sits in two decisions: which details to collect, and how to trust a change later. The seven steps follow the order payroll meets them, starting with the first hire.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick the payees first: employees on payroll, contractors paid by ACH, or both. The groups need different paperwork. Employees sign a deposit authorization, while a contractor also owes you a W-9 before the first payment goes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Every version needs the account holder's name, the bank name, the routing number, the account number and the account type. Show where to find them: the nine-digit routing number sits bottom left on a check, with the account number to its right.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for a voided check or a letter from the bank showing both numbers. Savings accounts rarely come with checks. For those, accept the bank letter or a pre-filled form printed from online banking.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Let employees add up to two more accounts, each with its own dollar amount or percentage. Require exactly one account to take whatever is left, and show the split on a sample paycheck before they sign.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Let the employee choose the bank
fields.howto_step_5_des: Under Regulation E, an employer can require direct deposit only when the employee picks the bank that receives it. Never tie the form to one bank, and file each signed authorization with the employee's payroll record.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Treat a request to switch accounts as unverified until the employee confirms it. Send that confirmation to contact details already on file, never to the email address or phone number written in the request itself.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Check that the first deposit lands
fields.howto_step_7_des: Ask each new hire to confirm the first deposit reached the right account. Keep a paper check ready for that payday in case it did not, and close the setup only after the employee says the money arrived.

plan.angle: The top 10 is bank PDFs and blank templates that collect numbers and check nothing. This page explains what the form asks for and where to get one, then builds what a PDF cannot: a form that checks the routing number as it is typed, reads the voided check, handles split deposits, and holds every bank change until the employee confirms it on a number already on file.
tab_stories: A new hire types a routing number and uploads a voided check, the app reads the check, finds one digit different and sends the form back to the new hire before payroll ever sees it.
An employee sends $150 of each paycheck to savings and the rest to checking, and the form shows the split against a sample net pay so the numbers add up before they sign.
A request to switch an employee's deposit account is held, a code goes to the phone number already in the HR record, and the payroll manager gets a direct message once it is confirmed.
Contractors submit bank details together with a W-9, and any account whose holder name does not match the W-9 name waits for accounts payable before the first payout.
